t: A duchy of the Holy Roman Empire centred on Leuven, Brussels and Antwerp, among the most urbanised lands of medieval Europe.
Its Joyous Entry of 1356 bound every new duke to respect the estates' rights and was sworn by Burgundian and Habsburg rulers alike.
Antwerp made it Europe's commercial hub in the 1500s; the Dutch Revolt split it, and France annexed the rest in 1795.
dyk: Duke John I of Brabant, victor at Worringen in 1288, was also a poet: love songs under his name survive in the famous Codex Manesse of German lyric poetry.
ev: The Diet of Schwäbisch Hall confirms Henry I's ducal rank over Brabant
John I wins the Battle of Worringen and gains the Duchy of Limburg
Duchess Joanna and Wenceslaus swear the Joyous Entry charter
Philip the Good of Burgundy inherits Brabant
Antwerp opens its new commercial exchange
Alexander Farnese captures Antwerp; the Dutch close the Scheldt
The Peace of Münster confirms the split of Brabant between Spain and the Dutch Republic
The French Republic annexes the duchy
